relevance_reason: The paper reports biallelic SMO loss-of-function variants in 7 individuals from 5 families with a developmental disorder that includes hypothalamic hamartoma and postaxial polydactyly (a Pallister-Hall-like spectrum). It also includes functional studies in patient-derived cells.

findings.statement: Le et al. (2020) reported 7 individuals from 5 independent families with a wide spectrum of developmental anomalies. These affected the brain (hypothalamic hamartoma and microcephaly), the heart (atrioventricular septal defect), the skeleton (postaxial polydactyly, narrow chest, and shortening of long bones), and the enteric nervous system (aganglionosis).
quotes: we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families; these variations cause a wide phenotypic spectrum of developmental anomalies affecting the brain (hypothalamic hamartoma and microcephaly), heart (atrioventricular septal defect), skeleton (postaxial polydactyly, narrow chest, and shortening of long bones), and enteric nervous system (aganglionosis)

findings.statement: In 7 affected individuals from 5 independent families with developmental anomalies, Le et al. (2020) identified biallelic loss-of-function variants in the SMO gene. The abstract does not list the individual variants.
quotes: Here, we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families

findings.statement: Le et al. (2020) found that cells from affected individuals had normal ciliogenesis but severely altered hedgehog signal transduction. This resulted either from altered trafficking at the primary cilium or from abnormal activation of the pathway downstream of SMO. GLI2 accumulated at the ciliary tip independently of hedgehog stimulation, which the authors suggested points to a role for SMO in regulating basal ciliary trafficking of GLI2 when the pathway is off.
quotes: Cells derived from affected individuals showed normal ciliogenesis but severely altered Hh-signal transduction as a result of either altered PC trafficking or abnormal activation of the pathway downstream of SMO.
Hh-independent GLI2 accumulation at the PC tip in cells from the affected individuals suggests a potential function of SMO in regulating basal ciliary trafficking of GLI2 when the pathway is off.

relevance_reason: Reports two brothers with familial hypothalamic hamartomas and polydactyly attributed to germline SMO mutations, a Pallister-Hall-like syndrome distinct from GLI3-related PHS.

findings.statement: Rubino et al. (2019) described 2 brothers with a familial syndrome of hypothalamic hamartomas and polydactyly that differed from Pallister-Hall syndrome. One brother had a large hypothalamic hamartoma that was biopsied and subtotally resected by an endoscopic endonasal approach, and the authors reported its histopathologic findings.
quotes: In this clinical report, the authors describe two brothers with a different familial syndrome.
The authors discuss the endoscopic endonasal biopsy and subtotal resection of a large hypothalamic hamartoma in one of the patients as well as the histopathological findings encountered.

findings.statement: Rubino et al. (2019) attributed the familial syndrome of hypothalamic hamartomas and polydactyly in 2 brothers to germline mutations in the SMO gene. They stated that this was the first familial syndrome reported to be caused by germline SMO mutations, and the first familial syndrome other than Pallister-Hall syndrome to be associated with hypothalamic hamartomas.
quotes: To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first report in the literature describing a familial syndrome caused by germline mutations in the Smoothened (SMO) gene and the first familial syndrome associated with hypothalamic hamartomas other than Pallister-Hall syndrome.

findings.statement: Rubino et al. (2019) contrasted the syndrome in their family, which they attributed to germline SMO mutations, with Pallister-Hall syndrome. They noted that Pallister-Hall syndrome is autosomal dominant and is caused by truncation of GLI3, a downstream effector in the sonic hedgehog pathway.
quotes: These tumors are most often sporadic but rarely can be associated with Pallister-Hall syndrome, an autosomal dominant familial syndrome caused by truncation of glioblastoma transcription factor 3, a downstream effector in the sonic hedgehog pathway.

relevance_reason: The paper studies hypothalamic hamartoma, the key lesion shared with Pallister-Hall syndrome. It reports somatic GLI3 locus abnormalities in tissue from sporadic, nonsyndromic HH and no causative germline GLI3 mutations. This gives context on the genetic basis of HH in patients without germline GLI3 defects.

findings.statement: Craig et al. (2008) studied 55 patients with sporadic, nonsyndromic hypothalamic hamartoma and intractable epilepsy, comparing genomic DNA from peripheral blood with DNA from surgically resected HH tissue. Resequencing of GLI3 found no causative germline mutations.
quotes: We isolated genomic DNA from peripheral blood and surgically resected HH tissue in 55 patients with sporadic HH and intractable epilepsy.
Resequencing of GLI3 did not identify causative germline mutations

findings.statement: Craig et al. (2008) found somatic (tumor-only) chromosomal abnormalities involving the GLI3 locus in 8 of 55 (15%) resected hypothalamic hamartoma tissue samples. Copy-number analysis on Affymetrix 10K SNP arrays identified a somatic abnormality on chromosome 7p in one sample. GLI3 resequencing showed loss of heterozygosity (LOH) within GLI3 in 3 samples, and genotyping of 28 SNPs in and around GLI3 found LOH in 5 more. The authors concluded that these somatic GLI3 abnormalities are associated with HH pathogenesis in sporadic, nonsyndromic patients, and noted that the abnormalities appeared highly variable.
quotes: we identified a somatic chromosomal abnormality on chromosome 7p in one HH tissue sample.
did identify LOH within the GLI3 gene in the HH tissue samples of three patients. Further genotyping of 28 SNPs within and surrounding GLI3 identified five additional patients exhibiting LOH.
Chromosomal abnormalities including the GLI3 locus were seen in 8 of 55 (15%) of the resected HH tissue samples. These somatic mutations appear to be highly variable.

findings.statement: Craig et al. (2008) described hypothalamic hamartomas as rare, benign congenital tumors associated with intractable epilepsy. Most cases are sporadic and nonsyndromic, and about 5% are associated with Pallister-Hall syndrome, which is caused by haploinsufficiency of GLI3.
quotes: Hypothalamic hamartomas (HH) are rare, benign congenital tumors associated with intractable epilepsy. Most cases are sporadic and nonsyndromic. Approximately 5% of HH cases are associated with Pallister-Hall syndrome (PHS), which is caused by haploinsufficiency of GLI3.

relevance_reason: Early report of two cases of hypothalamic hamartoma with associated developmental defects, the core combination in Pallister-Hall-like phenotypes. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: MARCUSE et al. (1953) reported 2 cases of hamartoma of the hypothalamus with associated developmental defects.
quotes: Hamartoma of the hypothalamus; report of two cases with associated developmental defects.

relevance_reason: Describes fetuses with congenital hypothalamic hamartoma and skeletal dysplasia, a possibly familial form distinct from Pallister-Hall syndrome, and proposes minimum diagnostic criteria for it.

findings.statement: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) reported congenital hypothalamic hamartomas found at autopsy in 3 unrelated fetuses. In 2 of the fetuses the tumor was associated only with skeletal dysplasia. In the third it was part of a nonrandom association of congenital malformations suggestive of Meckel syndrome.
quotes: We report on congenital hypothalamic hamartomas, discovered at autopsy in 3 unrelated fetuses.
In the first 2 patients, the tumor was associated with skeletal dysplasia only.
In the third patient, it was part of a non-random congenital malformation association, suggestive of Meckel syndrome.

findings.statement: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) noted that in one family, a previous boy had died soon after birth with similar craniofacial and skeletal abnormalities. They suggested the disorder may be familial.
quotes: In one family, a previous boy died soon after birth with similar craniofacial and skeletal abnormalities.
a nosologically distinct, possibly familial entity

findings.statement: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) reviewed reported cases of Pallister-Hall syndrome and found that only skeletal dysplasia and orofacial abnormalities were consistently present, resembling the findings in their first 2 cases. They proposed these features as the minimum criteria for a distinct, possibly familial entity, which they suggested calling 'congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome' (CHHS).
quotes: A detailed analysis of the PHS reported cases shows that only skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities are present constantly.

These findings prompt us to consider skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities as common denominator and minimum criteria required to define a nosologically distinct, possibly familial entity, which we suggest calling "congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome" (CHHS).
